Design deviation recorded: bunx multi-package limitation in Bun 1.4.0 ('bunx -p pkg1 -p pkg2 cmd' fails to link non-binary packages, so commitlint cannot resolve @commitlint/config-conventional ephemerally). Solution keeps pins only in the justfile: 'tools' target provisions both packages into target/dev-tools (gitignored, stamp-guarded .pins), and commit-check refreshes a byte-identical copy of commitlint.config.ts there because commitlint resolves extends relative to the config file directory, not cwd. BG-3 decision: literal peak-memory ceiling, not resident-decoded-bytes. RFC-0001 verification obligation requires a pre-allocation rejection test proving peak memory stays under BG-3, so the decode path must not allocate a second full-size buffer. Fix: replace load_from_memory_with_format().to_rgba8() (which clones even RGBA8 at image 0.25.9) with a per-format ImageDecoder that decodes into exactly one width*height*4 RGBA8 allocation, expanding L8/La8/Rgb8 channels in place. Native 16-bit and other non-8-bit decoder color types are rejected defensively (16-bit PNG already rejected at sniff). BG-2 (4096x4096) and BG-3 (64 MiB) are unchanged for all accepted formats; no accepted invariant is weakened. Regression test uses a thread-local tracking global allocator to measure peak allocation for PNG-RGBA, PNG-RGB, JPEG-RGB and WebP-RGBA at 4096x4096. Before: 8 B/px RGBA-native (128 MiB) and 7 B/px RGB-native (112 MiB). After target: <= 4 B/px plus bounded encoded input and codec scratch.

RFC-0001/OQ-042 impact needing review: to make BG-3 a literal peak guarantee for every accepted image, the pre-allocation estimate now charges 8 bytes per pixel for static WebP without a direct RGBA8 write (VP8 lossy, VP8X, and VP8L without the alpha bit), instead of the table value w*h*4. image-webp allocates a full-size internal RGBA scratch buffer when has_alpha is false (measured 8.00 B/px lossless RGB) and decoder planes for VP8 (measured 5.62 B/px lossy RGB). Consequence: a 4096x4096 non-alpha WebP is now rejected with DecodedTooLarge; its largest accepted square side is 2896. 3840x2160 (4K) lossy WebP still fits (about 63.3 MiB estimate). This is a tightening, not a weakening, but it revises the BG-3 formula for WebP and must be reflected in RFC-0001 or explicitly reverted to a codec-scratch-excluded reading. Second residual: the 8 B/px factor is derived from image-webp 0.2.4 internals and could drift on dependency upgrades; the regression test pins the measured behavior. CONFIRMED residual race: UnixStream::peer_addr returns the connect-time path string, not the connected socket inode, so the post-connect stat reads whatever inode now occupies that path. A local attacker can bind a spoof before connect and restore the vetted inode before the client re-stat, making verify_connected_endpoint pass while the live connection still reaches the spoof (reproduced in /tmp/opencode/pt2). This narrows but does not close the checked-then-swapped window; only SO_PEERCRED or a challenge/response removes it. Documented in serve.rs and the PR residual section. Follow-up: allow bitty-ipc to use the already-locked rustix socket_peercred (safe, Linux) or CTX-0159 SO_PEERCRED seam.

NEEDS-FIX P1-5: the whole-versus-bytewise STATE equality assertion is implied by the action equality assertion and therefore adds no discriminating power over it. fuzz_targets/terminal_state.rs first asserts whole.retained == chunked.retained, then runs run_replay(bytes, whole) and run_replay(bytes, chunked) and asserts the ReplayResults are equal. run_replay is a pure function of (data, actions) and bytes is identical in both calls, so once retained is proven equal the state equality follows. P1-1 control wait can block for twice the pinned CTL_TIMEOUT: in both enqueue_control_and_wait and enqueue_control_and_wait_with_connection, the recv_timeout error arm calls ticket.cancel, which only succeeds from Queued or Claimed. Once the drain has called begin_apply (phase Applying), cancel returns false and the waiter performs a SECOND full CTL_TIMEOUT wait. CTL_TIMEOUT is 5s and is pinned by ctl_timeout_budget_is_pinned, and the client reuses the same constant for its socket read and write timeouts in ctl/client.rs. Net effect: a control whose apply phase is in flight holds the connection worker for up to 10s while the client abandons at 5s, and the reply for an already-applied effect is replaced by Unavailable. No test asserts elapsed time on this path; the only ticket test asserts cancel on a queued item.

P1-2 the process-wide shared rate limiter replaces the per-connection budget: ipc_serve now constructs one RateLimiter::rc9_default in unix_serve and passes Arc<Mutex<RateLimiter>> to every connection, replacing the per-connection limiter in serve_stream. One abusive client can exhaust the shared budget and starve every other client, all requests serialize on one mutex, and serve_connection_with_shared_limiter maps lock poison to Unavailable with NO PoisonError::into_inner recovery, the pattern used everywhere else in this codebase (global_control_queue, ChildOwnership, automation_store). A single panic in any connection thread holding the limiter therefore denies all IPC traffic for the process lifetime. If a process-wide budget is intended it needs a decision record plus poison recovery. Note MAX_AUTHORITY_SESSIONS 64 exceeds RC9_MAX_CONNECTIONS 16, so the authority cap is correctly not the binding constraint.

P1-3 the debug read surface silently gains a second scope requirement, and P1-4 the capability-bearing param is parsed by hand. require_debug_read_scope was replaced by require_debug_terminal_capability, which requires a debug scope AND terminal.inspect, contradicting the deleted contract comment that debug.control is a superset of debug.trace which is a superset of debug.inspect so any debug scope may read. It does not break production only because ScopeSet::cli_default already contains terminal.inspect and elevation_from_env is additive-only so the scope can never be absent. The divergence is papered over in a pub test constructor: with_granted_session inserts Scope::TerminalInspect into capability_scopes, silently widening the terminal capability of every hermetic context. Separately, request_terminal_id extracts terminalId by substring search on the raw params and takes the next colon and next quote; it can match a key appearing inside a string value via an escaped quote, silently ignores a second occurrence, and does not agree with the parser the handler itself uses. The value only selects a capability-map key so the blast radius today is a mis-targeted check, but it is a security decision input and the repo already has real parsers in ctl.rs (parse_terminal_id_params, parse_send_params). P1-8 LifecycleGate is not panic-safe and permanently wedges the runtime: suspend, resume, and dispose all do enter, then run the inner fn, then leave, and leave is NOT in a scope guard. A panic inside the inner fn leaves transition.active set forever, after which every suspend, resume, and dispose fails with lifecycle transition already in progress and invoke_command and deliver_event fail or return 0 unconditionally, with no recovery path. Use a scopeguard or explicit re-arm. restore_after_suspend and restore_after_resume have the same shape and additionally clear self.lifecycle_fault only on the success path. P1-9 suspend and resume mutate host and pipeline in OPPOSITE order: suspend_with commits registry.suspend then pipeline.detach_plugin, while resume_inner commits pipeline.attach_subscriptions then registry.resume then registry.activate. Each ordering leaves a window in which a crash or abort leaves a SUSPENDED PLUGIN STILL ATTACHED TO EVENT QUEUES, and there is no write-ahead record or roll-forward, so the transaction is atomic against returned errors only. The LifecycleGate does not close this because PluginRuntime is not Send (it holds Rc<RefCell<ServiceDirectory>>) and lives on the main thread, so nothing else can run inside the window; the window is reachable only by an abort. Document the boundary as error-atomic, not crash-atomic, or add a roll-forward record.

P1-10 total_dropped is now non-monotonic across purge: EventPipeline.detach_plugin moves per-queue drop counts into detached_drops, but purge_plugin deletes both the queues and the detached_drops entries, and remove, dispose, and reload all call purge_plugin. total_dropped and dropped_per_queue therefore DECREASE across a remove or reload cycle, and the counter feeds Runtime accounting at runtime.rs line 911. If any bound or health signal derives from a cumulative drop total, a remove or reload cycle resets it. Keep purged accounting by tombstoning the key, or document the metric as per-generation rather than cumulative. P1-4 (NEW, upgraded from the previous round's P2(c)): bearer-token entropy diverges by platform. crates/bitty-ipc/src/devtools/automation.rs random_bearer_token reads 16 bytes from /dev/urandom on unix; the #[cfg(not(unix))] arm concatenates two RandomState::build_hasher().finish() values. Measured directly: the tokens are NOT constant - RandomState keys are a per-thread base incremented per call, so successive calls and successive processes produce distinct values, so there is no constant-token bug. But the token is a deterministic function of (per-thread base key, call index) rather than a CSPRNG output, and the second half carries no independent entropy. The unix path has 128 CSPRNG bits; the Windows path has materially less and is structurally derived. A bearer is the authority token for automation synthesize, capture and frame-digest. Upgraded from P2 to P1 because this is a security control on a supported platform - the ConPTY backend, crates/bitty-pty/tests/spawn_windows.rs and the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu CI job all exist. Fix: use a CSPRNG on every platform.

P1-3 (open): suspend and resume commit in opposite orders, and the boundary is undocumented. Host::suspend_with commits registry.suspend(id) and then pipeline.detach_plugin(id); resume_inner commits pipeline.attach_subscriptions(...), then registry.resume(id), then registry.activate(id). Each ordering leaves a window in which an abort leaves a SUSPENDED plugin still attached to its event queues, and there is no write-ahead record or roll-forward. The before_commit seam plus the new restore_after_* rollbacks and the attach_subscriptions pre-validation give real ERROR-atomicity; they do not give crash-atomicity. PluginRuntime is not Send (it holds Rc<RefCell<ServiceDirectory>>) and lives on the main thread, so nothing else can run inside the window - the window is reachable only by an abort. The doc comments ('/// Suspend a plugin.', '/// Resume a suspended plugin into the registered state.') state no atomicity scope, and issue 1410's title says 'atomic' unqualified. Fix: document the boundary as error-atomic, and either narrow the issue title or add a roll-forward record. Unchanged from the previous round.

C1 (P1, open, independently confirmed): reader cancellation is silently dropped inside the try_wait window. crates/bitty-pty/src/platform/mod.rs:119-129 cancel returns Ok(()) unless state == Active AND the generation matches; begin_try_wait at :186 sets state = Reaping WITHOUT advancing the generation. A cancel landing while imp::try_wait is in flight is accepted, reports success, and never invokes the killer. ReadCancellation.cancelled is still set so a pump between reads exits at its next check, but a pump already blocked inside read is released only by the child dying, which the dropped cancel prevents. PtyReader::join then burns its 2s deadline and returns a retained reader. Bounded and reportable rather than silent, and untested because the window is a single waitpid(WNOHANG). Fix: queue the pending cancellation across the reap window, or return WouldBlock so the caller retries. Unchanged from the previous two rounds.

C5 (P2, NEW): begin_wait violates the invariant its sibling documents. begin_kill states the rule in its own comment - advance the generation first because it is the only fallible step, so a rejected claim cannot strand the record half-transitioned - and honours it. begin_wait at platform/mod.rs:213-224 does the opposite: it sets state = Reaping and action = None and only then calls the fallible advance_generation. On overflow (u64::MAX, unreachable in practice) Session::wait returns Err before finish_wait, permanently stranding the record in Reaping with action = None, after which every kill/try_wait/wait returns ChildAlreadyReaped and every cancel becomes a no-op. Fail-closed, so low severity, but it is exactly the half-transitioned shape the neighbouring function is written to avoid. Fix: apply begin_kill ordering.

G1 (P1, SECURITY, open, independently confirmed): bearer-token entropy is platform-divergent and the weak branch is the Windows production path. random_bearer_token at crates/bitty-ipc/src/devtools/automation.rs:136-172 has two implementations. Unix at :137-154 reads 16 bytes from /dev/urandom, giving 128 bits hex-encoded. Non-unix at :155-172 calls RandomState::new().build_hasher().finish() twice and concatenates the result into the same 16 bytes. RandomState is SipHash keyed by a per-process/per-thread counter-derived seed, built for hash-DoS resistance and not for secrecy; two calls in one thread yield k and k+1-ish keys, so the output is a deterministic function of the process initial seed and carries far less than 128 bits of unpredictable entropy. These bearers are the capability token for Synthesize, Capture and FrameDigest, the debug-control surface. The Unix path was clearly hardened and the Windows path was left on the pre-existing weak source. Fix: use a CSPRNG on every platform (getrandom or rand rngs OsRng) and delete the cfg split. P1-2 (P1, open, independently confirmed): LifecycleGate is not panic-safe and permanently wedges the runtime. crates/bitty-runtime/src/plugin_runtime/mod.rs:1205 (suspend), :1275 (resume) and :1359 (dispose) all do transition.enter(op, id)? then run the inner fn then transition.leave(), and leave is not in a scope guard. No profile in Cargo.toml sets panic = abort - I checked every profile table - so a panic unwinds and transition.active stays Some(op) permanently, after which every suspend, resume and dispose for EVERY plugin returns "lifecycle transition already in progress" while invoke_command and deliver_event fail or return 0 unconditionally. There is no recovery path. The inner functions reach Rc<RefCell<LuaVm>> and Rc<RefCell<ServiceDirectory>>, so a RefCell borrow conflict panics readily, and crates/bitty-plugin-host/tests/safe_recovery.rs shows panics are a considered failure mode here. restore_after_suspend and restore_after_resume have the same shape and additionally clear self.lifecycle_fault only on the success path. Fix: a scopeguard-style RAII guard that calls leave() on drop. Unchanged from the previous two rounds.

P1-3 (P2, DOWNGRADED from the previous round P1 with corrected analysis): the suspend/resume commit-order asymmetry is error-atomic, not broken, so the previous P1 framing does not hold. Host::suspend_with at crates/bitty-plugin-host/src/host.rs:398-420 commits registry.suspend(id) then pipeline.detach_plugin(id), and detach_plugin returns usize rather than Result, so the second step cannot fail and suspend is trivially atomic on the error path. resume_inner at :435 commits attach_subscriptions then registry.resume then registry.activate and carries BOTH compensating arms (a registry.resume error triggers detach_plugin, an activate error triggers registry.suspend). That satisfies the task description wording "roll back or complete exactly once on errors", and issue 1410 title is "transactional", not "atomic" - the previous note misquoted it. The genuine residual is that crash-atomicity is claimed nowhere and the seam is named before_commit, implying a two-phase commit that does not exist. Fix: document the boundary as error-atomic and rename or re-document the seam.

P2-2 (P2, open): total_dropped is still non-monotonic across purge_plugin. Blast radius is limited to the plugin_pipeline_dropped debug-trace field at crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime.rs:910 and the Runtime::plugin_total_dropped observability accessor, used by bitty plugin doctor and three tests. No budget or health signal derives from it, so this is metric correctness rather than a control failure - P2 is the right severity. C1 / PX-3598 / PX-3622 / PX-3648 fixed: a try_wait window no longer disables reader cancellation. ChildOwnership::cancel now decides on the record state instead of requiring Active, so a cancellation landing while a poll owns the record is recorded as owed (ChildOwnershipData::cancel_owed) rather than reported Ok(()) and dropped. begin_try_wait deliberately does NOT rotate the generation and does NOT take the cancellation action, and its comment now states why: a poll reaps nothing, so the child is still alive and every reader that captured a generation must stay cancellable. That also keeps Session::reader_cancel correct when it is called inside the window, because a rotate-and-restore generation would orphan a reader that captured the window value. The obligation is coordinated under the same single lock as the state transition, so cancel and finish_try_wait cannot interleave into a lost or duplicated signal. On ReapOutcome::Running the owed request is claimed exactly like a kill (action taken, state moved to Killing), so the dying child is never signalled twice; a platform refusal rolls that claim back under abort_kill's rules (state, action and generation restored, the child stays cancellable and a later kill re-claims) and returns the error to the poll caller, the only observer of a deferred delivery. finish_try_wait therefore returns io::Result<()> and Session::try_wait propagates it; it can never mask the poll result, because a terminal outcome (Reaped or Failed) retires the record without delivering anything. On a terminal outcome the owed request dies with the record: that child is unreachable through the ownership record and the poll outcome is already reported. Kill ownership and rollback are otherwise unchanged: begin_kill/abort_kill keep their ordering and their refusal to resurrect a reaped child, and a window is only ever closed by its own finish_try_wait (begin_kill and begin_wait still return ChildAlreadyReaped while a poll is in flight, so no cross-closing is possible).

New error surface introduced by the C1 fix, outside this task's file scope: Pty::try_wait (and therefore Pty::wait_timeout) can now return Err for a deferred reader cancellation the platform refused, where before the same refusal was dropped inside the poll window. Production consumers were not changed and each already collapses try_wait errors conservatively: crates/bitty-runtime/src/execution/registry.rs:1780 maps any Err to exited (which then runs kill+reap through terminate), crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/pty.rs:445 discards it with .ok()?, and crates/bitty-pty/src/pty.rs wait_timeout propagates it. The refusal can only happen when the child killer itself failed, i.e. the child is already dying or unreachable, so no consumer becomes less safe; it is recorded because a reviewer should confirm that reading rather than inherit it. C2/C3/C4/C5/C6/C7 (PX-3649 through PX-3654) were deliberately NOT touched in this pass: begin_wait still mutates before its fallible advance_generation, the new pub API is still undocumented, the sole production join() call site still discards PtyReaderJoinError, the wl-copy PATH-isolation proof still self-skips, and the SIGKILL doc claim is still inaccurate. Batch-review P1 fixed. Root cause of the P1: winit raises AboutToWait once per dispatch cycle (wayland/event_loop/mod.rs:515) and the embedder ticks on it, but a compositor may flush the commit and the echoing wl_keyboard key in two consecutive wl_display roundtrips, so releasing the claim at the commit batch tick handed the echo straight back to the terminal. ImeKeyClaim:***REDACTED*** now carries an absolute echo_by deadline (IME_COMMIT_ECHO_WINDOW, 250ms, re-exported from lib.rs) instead of being tick-scoped: tick_at ages it, the observation of the echo spends it, and only the elapsed window releases it. A tick count cannot work because a tick only happens when something arrives and the keystroke that must not be lost is the next thing to arrive.

Preserved behaviours, each pinned by a test: live composition still absorbs every raw press including repeats and survives any number of ticks; a repeat press is never the echo so it neither spends nor waits on the claim, while Composing still absorbs repeats (CTX-0367 unchanged); Esc cancel (empty preedit, no commit) absorbs its own raw Esc exactly once then hands the keyboard straight back; focus loss and Ime::Disabled force-release the claim; commit text is still never trimmed. Clock seams added in the house style: handle_ime_preedit_at and handle_ime_commit_at, mirroring tick_at/handle_cursor_moved_at, so every deadline test is hermetic and no test sleeps.

Test suite now 29 hermetic cases in crates/bitty-runtime/tests/ime_input.rs, all synthetic event orderings, no personal input data. New batch-order coverage: commit_echo_in_the_next_batch_is_still_absorbed (the P1), commit_echo_stays_absorbed_across_several_ticks, presented_and_skipped_frames_alike_do_not_release_the_claim_early, commit_claim_expires_once_the_echo_window_elapses, idle_after_commit_does_not_absorb_the_next_keystroke (X11 shape with no tick at all), wayland_commit_and_echo_in_one_batch_still_absorbs_the_echo, ***REDACTED***, a_repeat_press_never_spends_or_waits_on_the_commit_claim, a_repeat_press_is_still_absorbed_during_composition, esc_cancel_absorbs_its_own_echo_then_hands_the_keyboard_back. Mutation-verified the new regressions, each mutation caught and then reverted: tick force-releases the claim (the exact P1 defect) -> 4 failures incl. commit_echo_in_the_next_batch_is_still_absorbed; key path ignores the deadline -> 1 failure (idle_after_commit_does_not_absorb_the_next_keystroke); repeats spend the claim -> 1 failure; Composing stops absorbing raw keys -> 9 failures. Scope: added crates/bitty-runtime/src/lib.rs (re-export of the bound, lib.rs:261) so all 6 touched files are in recorded task scope; task scope list now 8 entries.

Accepted residual, now bounded and stated rather than open-ended: on a backend that filters the committing key outright (X11 XIM), the claim stays armed for up to IME_COMMIT_ECHO_WINDOW after the commit, so a keystroke typed inside that window is absorbed and the user must retype it. 250 ms is far above any compositor echo latency and far below any human inter-key interval, so the window is only reachable by a machine-speed keystroke. The alternative - releasing at the first tick - is the P1 defect: it reinstates the #1449 trailing space on any compositor that flushes the two halves separately. Chosen trade: never silently insert a byte the IME already committed, at the cost of at most one retype on a filtering backend.

An empty commit inserts nothing is a statement about the committed text, not about the echo. Accepted residuals, re-confirmed and correctly bounded. On a backend that filters the committing key outright (X11 XIM) the claim stays armed for up to IME_COMMIT_ECHO_WINDOW after the commit, so a keystroke typed inside that window is absorbed and must be retyped; 250 ms is far above any compositor echo latency and far below any human inter-key interval, so the window is only reachable by a machine-speed keystroke, and the alternative (release at the first tick) is the P1 defect - the trade is stated in the code and is the right way round. Key repeat immediately after a commit: the claim is one-shot, so held-key repeats would insert; pre-existing shape, fcitx5 does not commit repeatedly. Behaviour change needing a release-note line: a cancel (Esc) during composition now absorbs its own raw key, and the CTX-0367 test raw_keys_during_composition_do_not_double_input was rewritten because its assertion encoded the #1449 defect. Finding 1 implemented in fuzz/fuzz_targets/terminal_state.rs. The state layer is now driven interleaved: one Parser plus one State per chunk plan, every emitted action applied to the live state immediately, with the canonical state hash folded into a per-action digest. Four plans are compared against the whole-stream plan: whole, every-byte, mid-transition (exactly one interior boundary, provably inside a multi-byte construct, re-derived from the bytes so the plan cannot silently degenerate), and data-derived. Compared fields are applied-action count, per-action state digest, drained reply digest, pending-reply hash, and the canonical final state hash. The retained action-vector comparison is now a separate, clearly labelled parser-level property that runs after the state assertions. A real state-relevant seam was found while building this: a full reset discards the pending reply queue, so the host drain schedule is itself observable in the state; the drain policy is therefore pinned identically for every plan and a separate monotonic drain-schedule assertion records the behaviour. Bounded smoke is clean at max_len 64, 512, and 8192.

Round 2 P2 residual fixed. Root cause of finding I3: handle_ime_commit_at released the claim whenever the commit string was empty, so a Composing or CommitKey claim plus an empty commit went to Free and the raw committing key reached the PTY, which is the issue 1449 shape on the cancel ordering. The old comment was inconsistent: it argued correctly that the raw key is still in flight at the commit, then released on emptiness, which is a statement about the inserted text and not about the echo. Fix is one rule in input.rs: a commit whose claim is Free stays Free (unsolicited, owns no key), and a commit whose claim is Composing or CommitKey arms a deadline-bounded CommitKey whatever the string is, re-stamped from the commit because the commit is the last IME evidence of the gesture. No documented contract requires the empty commit to release; winit states nothing about empty commit semantics and the echo is owed for the keystroke regardless of the string. The cost is the same already accepted residual as a filtering backend with a non-empty commit: at most one absorbed keystroke inside a 250 ms window.

I3 FIXED in code. The empty commit no longer releases the claim, so the cancel path (Esc, or Backspace clearing a selection) owes its raw key the same one-shot deadline-bounded claim as a full commit and cannot reinstate the issue 1449 trailing space. Chose survival over a documented exception because no contract requires the release: winit documents nothing about empty commit semantics, and the echo is owed for the keystroke, which the committed string does not describe. The unsolicited-commit guard is kept, because a commit with no composition behind it has no announced preedit and therefore no keystroke to owe.

CTX-0794 root cause identified precisely: cursor_to_cell() in crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/layout_focus.rs returns cell coordinates LOCAL to the currently-focused panes own terminal grid (self.state.snapshot() is swapped per focused pane via the pane-swap mechanism), while layout_allocations() returns view bounds in the CONTAINER GLOBAL coordinate space. PR #1474 record_selection_origin() and the drag-clamp code compare a local-space cursor_to_cell() position against global-space layout_allocations() bounds -- a coordinate-space mismatch, not a test-setup bug (confirmed after independently fixing two real test bugs: unused imports and a missing explicit set_container call, tests still fail 3 of 5 afterward with clearly wrong clamp targets, e.g. col 30 in the right panel clamping to 5 instead of 20). Correct fix direction: use the existing cursor_to_leaf_cell() helper (layout_focus.rs, already does proper global-to-local mapping via layout_allocations()) consistently for both hit-testing the origin panel AND converting motion positions, comparing everything in one coordinate space, OR keep everything in global cell space and only convert to pane-local at the final self.state lookup. This is a real architecture-level fix, not a one-line patch; recommend a dedicated implementation pass reading cursor_to_leaf_cell, update_selection, and update_block_selection together before re-attempting. PR #1474 must stay NEEDS-FIX/unmerged; PR #1473 also stays NEEDS-FIX (no-op, wrong issue content).

CTX-0794 precise root cause confirmed via instrumented debug run: after LayoutNode reflow, the single shared self.state terminal grid (Runtime.state) gets resized to the FOCUSED panes own decorated CONTENT area in cells (observed 17x22 for a nominal 20x24 View, i.e. shrunk by border/content_inset/gaps_out converted back to cells) -- NOT the View nominal cols/rows and NOT the global container/layout_allocations Rect space. clamp_cell_pos() in selection.rs clamps against this small local-content snapshot (max_col=16 in the observed run), which fires BEFORE the PR #1474 origin-bounds clamp (bounds.right()-1=19) ever gets a chance to matter -- so the two clamps operate in different, incompatible coordinate spaces (focused-pane local decorated-content cells vs global un-decorated View-declared cells) and the outer one is silently a no-op ceiling. Fixing this correctly requires either: (a) tracking the origin panes own local content dims (from a state snapshot swap, not layout_allocations) and clamping in that pane local space consistently, using the existing pane-swap mechanism the same way update_selection does today for the focused pane, or (b) doing all clamping in one unified coordinate space by mapping cursor_to_leaf_cell local-cell results forward, never mixing with global Rect bounds. This is a real architecture-aware implementation task, not a follow-up-free quick patch; recommend scoping a dedicated CTX task read alongside crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/panes.rs (pane-swap) before the next implementation attempt. Review 725ce8c3: NEEDS-FIX. Blocking B1: stall bound evadable by an unbounded uncharged ESC flood inside a discarding (non-G) APC while a stream is open: parser.rs:242 (in-APC ESC + non-backslash while apc_discarding -> i+=1, no note_interleaved) and parser.rs:193 (held in-APC ESC across advance() while discarding skips next byte uncharged). Repro shape: ESC _ X ; then ESC ESC ESC ... forever (or 1-byte advance calls of ESC/x) keeps the stream pinned; contradicts AC2 and the kitty_apc.rs module doc claim that interleaved input is counted. Fix: charge note_interleaved(1) in both branches (also the held-ESC byte), plus a regression test. Non-blocking: N1 stale doc line kitty_apc.rs:882 (old more_flag doc now prefixes struct Continuation doc); N2 continuation_flags first-m-wins ignores a later malformed m= (kitty_apc.rs:906) while parse_control is last-wins and rejects malformed, consider rejecting duplicate/malformed m consistently; N3 a=d mid-stream aborts but the delete itself is not executed (deletes unsupported today; note for follow-up); N4 held ESC outside APC (parser.rs ~214) uncharged, bounded 1 per advance call, acceptable; N5 per-byte note_interleaved in hot path is an Option check next to a per-byte vte advance, negligible; N6 NotGraphics header charged once (len+1), payload bytes charged in discarding, no double charge since terminate_apc returns early on discarding. Budget after abort OK: abort clears current_final/decoded/pending, parser clear_apc_header releases header current. missing_m abort is consistent with fail-closed rules (last chunk must carry m=0). No hardcoded paths. Gates: cargo test -p bitty-vt --locked ok (130+1+5+1), clippy -D warnings ok, fmt --check ok; review target dir removed.

Reviewer addendum (non-blocking): N7 the stall bound is byte-based, not time-based: a silent writer, or one sending empty Gm=1 continuations (each resets interleaved at kitty_apc.rs:663 with zero payload growth), still pins the open stream indefinitely. Empty m=1 chunks are legitimate (chafa opener), so treat as a documented limitation or a follow-up task (e.g. cap consecutive empty continuations), not part of this fix.

sccache evaluation verdict: recommend against, not clearly net-positive. Baseline run 37202274934: job wall 9-10 min, compile 31s check plus 250s test-profile codegen inside the 373s nextest step, 120s test execution. All 25 Compiling lines are bitty-local crates with warm rust-cache restore in 25s. sccache removes codegen only; linking, test execution, cache transfer remain. Full-hit reruns are rare and net 1-2 min; typical new commits always miss bitty-terminal since build.rs stamps current SHA into BITTY_COMMIT, so expected saving is at most 1 min against a 30 min budget. Decisive blocker is cache capacity: gh cache list shows 13 live entries at about 13 GB against the 10 GB repo cap, so eviction churn is already happening; a Windows sccache store near 1 GB would degrade both hit rates. cache-workspace-crates true rejected per upstream docs and known stale-hit rebuild loops. Poisoning risk is low by design; size is the binding constraint. No files changed; worktree carryctx/ctx-0960 clean. Revisit only if cache cap is raised or an external backend is adopted, or the Windows job nears budget.

R1 ProviderCredentialConfig — moved credential_ref.rs to provider_credential.rs in S5 with deprecated shim (removed S7). Verbatim semantics: At most one field may resolve — both set denies as conflict at resolution, neither set resolves to no credential. Construction preserves both fields so conflict stays observable instead of rejected silently at parse time. Display/Debug quote reference names only, values never enter type. Construction gate: each ref must match kind (Env for api_key_env, Cmd for api_key_cmd) else deny. Narrow-only: overlay may keep each ref identical or remove it, never add rename or switch sources; check_provider_override checks both fields independently, any widening denies. Resolution: exclusive-or first, conflict denies before read; Env via injected lookup, missing/empty denies names-only; Cmd via bounded shell-free runner; values returned never logged, inject into child env only per ADR-0006. Bound MAX_CREDENTIAL_CMD_OUTPUT_BYTES 4096. Counterpart: bitty-ai credential adapter owning same semantics.

- GlyphBitmap stored in cache (cache.rs) as CachedGlyph::Bitmap
- Coverage format defined by CoveragePolicy (atlas.rs): Grayscale (1 B/px) or Subpixel (3 B/px)

- Next: Profile current grayscale prevalence and identify storage optimization point

Design/feasibility report: existing bitty_lua::config::ConfigEval::eval_config is bounded and no-host, but returns Core-specific ConfigData, so plugin settings need a generic API. Proposed bitty-lua API: pub enum PlainConfigValue { Nil, Bool(bool), Integer(i64), Number(f64), String(String), Table(BTreeMap<String, PlainConfigValue>), Array(Vec<PlainConfigValue>) }; pub struct PlainConfigLimits { source_bytes, instruction_budget, wall_budget_ms, memory_limit, max_depth, max_keys, max_values, max_string_bytes, max_aggregate_bytes }; pub trait PlainConfigEval { fn eval_plain_config(&mut self, source: &str, limits: PlainConfigLimits) -> Result<PlainConfigValue, PlainConfigError>; }. Internally reuse LuaVm drive_chunk/RC accounting, but add a dedicated config constructor using phodopus Lua::builder().memory_limit(...).build() and only approved pure computation globals; do not call install_host_module, with_module_root, or expose plugin services. Because current retained stdlib installs os.time/clock/date and phodopus Lua::core includes debug/package/require, the config constructor must use an explicit minimal stdlib installation or a phodopus API change: load only the needed base/string/table/math/utf8/coroutine primitives, then remove _G, debug, package, require, load/loadfile/dofile, os, io, and any host callbacks before execution. Safer API is a separate ConfigLuaVm wrapper that owns Lua and only exposes eval_plain_config; no public access to LuaVm host-install methods. Capture output inside one enter call into owned Rust data; reject non-table top-level returns, nil/non-string keys, functions/userdata/threads/metatables that affect raw extraction, cyclic/deep tables, duplicate/aggregate overflows, NaN/inf if numeric settings reject them. Intersect the resulting top-level string-key table in plugin_runtime::plugin_settings with manifest-declared SettingDecl keys; map Bool/Integer/String/Array(String) strictly to LuaValue, drop unknown/wrong types, and never pass config values to capability/grant code. Keep existing flat TOML parser and merge semantics as fallback. Path resolution in bitty-config: canonical $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bitty/plugins/<owner>.<name>.lua; short <name>.lua only if a bounded precomputed map from the complete installed/discovered PluginId set contains exactly one owner, otherwise do not apply alias and record bounded ambiguity diagnostic. If canonical and alias both exist, canonical wins and alias is reported shadowed. If neither applicable Lua exists, read legacy <owner>.<name>.toml; invalid/oversized/unreadable Lua fails closed to defaults/lower layer and does not activate TOML when a Lua file was present; absent Lua permits TOML fallback. Build path only from validated PluginId owner/name segments, no traversal. XDG/platform precedence remains config_dir_with_platform_env: XDG_CONFIG_HOME > APPDATA > HOME/.config > LOCALAPPDATA. Isolation proof: fresh VM per settings load, no shared globals/registry/module roots, no host module/callbacks, no IO/module resolver, hard source/heap/fuel/wall bounds, owned plain-data snapshot, manifest allowlist after execution, and fail-closed on every error/limit. Do not implement until commander confirms scope. Docs follow-up required in bitty-terminal-docs/configuration/lua-and-xdg.md and likely bitty-plugins-docs/runtime/lua-runtime-rfc.md; no docs edits in this paused phase.

Updated exact design: eval_config cannot be reused for plugin settings because ConfigData is Core-specific. Minimal implementation should add a generic bitty-lua ConfigLuaVm/plain-data API, not route plugin data through Core ConfigData. Suggested public signatures: pub enum PlainConfigValue { Bool(bool), Integer(i64), Number(f64), String(String), Table(BTreeMap<String, PlainConfigValue>), Array(Vec<PlainConfigValue>) }; pub struct PlainConfigLimits { pub source_bytes: usize, pub instruction_budget: u64, pub wall_budget_ms: u64, pub memory_limit: usize, pub max_depth: usize, pub max_keys: usize, pub max_values: usize, pub max_string_bytes: usize, pub max_aggregate_bytes: usize }; pub enum PlainConfigError { SourceTooLarge, Vm(VmError), Lua(String), Shape(String), Limit(String) }; pub struct ConfigLuaVm { private Lua/budget state }; impl ConfigLuaVm { pub fn with_limits(id: impl Into<String>, limits: PlainConfigLimits) -> Result<Self, VmError>; pub fn eval_plain_config(&mut self, source: &str) -> Result<PlainConfigValue, PlainConfigError>; }. Use fresh VM per load, shared drive_chunk accounting, source cap before compile, hard fuel/wall/memory limits, and one-enter owned snapshot. Only string-keyed map tables and contiguous integer-key arrays are accepted; top-level must be a plain table (or explicitly define nil as empty), no mixed keys, functions, userdata, threads, binary strings, cycles/metatables affecting extraction, NaN/inf, duplicate keys, depth/key/value/string/aggregate overflows. Then plugin_settings converts only Bool/Integer/String/String-array values matching declared SettingKind and drops all other keys; no config value is ever passed to grants/capabilities. Dependency impact: bitty-lua API plus tests; bitty-runtime already depends on bitty-lua and bitty-config, so no new dependency; bitty-config remains pure path/identity helper unless generic values are kept runtime-local. Critical implementation prerequisite: current LuaVm::with_budgets builds phodopus Lua::builder and installs bitty retained stdlib; current phodopus Lua::core baseline includes debug/package/require and retained stdlib adds os.time/clock/date. ConfigLuaVm must use a separate construction function that loads only approved pure libraries or a phodopus API change exposing selective core loading, and must not call install_host_module, with_module_root, or any plugin bridge. If using existing LuaVm internals, keep the new constructor private/typed so host-install methods cannot be reached through the config API; otherwise refactor shared budget driver over a private VM core. This is the isolation proof: no host callbacks, module roots, IO/network, require/package/debug/os, plugin services, or shared registry/globals; only pure computation and owned plain-data output. Path contract: canonical `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bitty/plugins/<owner>.<name>.lua`; alias `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bitty/plugins/<short-name>.lua` only from a bounded precomputed map over all installed/discovered valid PluginIds, exact one-to-one short-name ownership. If map unavailable/stale/ambiguous, alias is never applied and bounded diagnostic records the reason. Canonical existing wins; alias existence is reported shadowed. If no applicable Lua path exists, read legacy `<owner>.<name>.toml`; if Lua exists but is invalid/oversized/unreadable/evaluation fails, use defaults/lower settings and do not fall through to TOML. All path segments derive from validated PluginId; no traversal. Platform path uses existing config_dir_with_platform_env order XDG > APPDATA > HOME/.config > LOCALAPPDATA. NEEDS-FIX P1 security: crates/bitty-runtime/src/plugin_runtime/plugin_settings.rs:363-460 performs metadata/symlink checks, then std::fs::read on the path. A concurrent rename/symlink swap after the check can make the loader read an attacker-selected file; a FIFO/device can also make the supposedly bounded read block or consume unbounded data. Remediation: use a single safe open operation that refuses symlinks/non-regular files (platform-appropriate no-follow flags or equivalent), then read through a bounded reader and verify the opened file identity/length before evaluation; apply the same policy to the legacy TOML path if it remains in scope.

NEEDS-FIX P1 resource bound: crates/bitty-lua/src/plain_config.rs:330 collects the entire table.iter() into Vec before enforcing max_keys. A source can create many table entries within the 16 KiB source cap, causing a large native allocation and retaining all GC Values before the configured key/value/aggregate limits reject it. Remediation: iterate incrementally, reject once max_keys is reached, and avoid retaining the full pair vector; ensure table iteration itself is bounded and charges allocation/values before cloning.

NEEDS-FIX P1 precedence/security: crates/bitty-runtime/src/plugin_runtime/mod.rs:1940-1950 builds discovered_ids from self.entries only. Recommendation for 0.0.24: ship a contract-only additive UI v1.1 over existing mount/update. Keep exactly Text, Row, Column, List; add no Capsule, Button, Badge, Image, spacer, size, alignment, padding, radius, shadow, transition, tooltip, hover, or disabled node. Formally expose optional fields on every accepted node: fg string, bg string, bold boolean, on_click table {command string,args scalar table}, on_scroll table with same shape. Existing trees with none of these fields render identically. Band semantics: Text leaves concatenate; Row concatenates children; Column and List retain existing preorder inline flattening in horizontal bands, so no new vertical promise. Nearest ancestor style and binding inherit, leaf declaration wins. Reject unknown node kinds, wrong types, invalid token grammar, malformed command tables, functions, cyclic tables, duplicate args, and bounds with E_UI_COMPONENT_INVALID; invalid update keeps last-known-good tree. Use only the current bounded host token set foreground/background/cursor/selection/accent in 0.0.24; raw colors and plugin-owned chrome tokens are out. Unknown syntactically valid but unresolved token must fail at mount/update rather than silently paint default. Keep mount activation-only and update bounded mutation; no unmount/move API in this release. Handles are opaque positive generation-epoch plus counter values; suspend, dispose, crash, reload, safe-mode disable, or capability revocation clears blocks and revokes handles. Stale update returns false or typed unavailable; it never mutates another generation. Empty Text hides a band and reserves no row. Geometry is Core-owned, exclusive, and shared by paint/hit-test; content-only update damages the band only, while visibility/geometry changes reflow and resize PTY through ordinary path. Command rule: preserve bar init ordering by validating binding syntax at mount/update, then resolve same-generation registered command at dispatch; only owning plugin commands are allowed in 0.0.24, foreign or stale commands deny with no VM call. Click press consumes band, release fires only if same edge/surface/run/request, and queues max 8; on_scroll consumes only bound spans, injects signed delta, coalesces same target and saturates to 4096, with max 8 queue; all dispatch uses normal command registry and capability checks. No keyboard or IME focus enters chrome. Accessibility derives clickable Text as button with bounded accessible name from text; noninteractive Text is text, Row/Column/List group/list as appropriate; chrome is exposed read-only and excluded from tab order. Do not add accessibility authoring fields until the projection contract requires them. Recommend per-edge BAND_MAX_NODES_PER_FRAME=4096, counted over flattened nodes, with whole-surface truncation marker and diagnostic on overflow; retain per-block 2048 nodes, depth 16, text 256 KiB, 64 blocks and 2 MiB aggregate per generation, 16 args and 256-byte scalar strings. Per-frame updates should be coalesced to one present per plugin per tick and never run Lua on input/render hot path.

## Security review CTX-1377 / PR #2289 (head 7ba4cc77) — VERDICT: APPROVE

No blocking findings. Independent review (agent spawn-review); no push/merge.

### Defect (PX-7488 / #2287) and fix
- Confirm: std allocates its CLOEXEC exec-error pipe inside `Command::spawn` at the lowest free descriptors before fork. With 3/4 free, the `pre_exec` `dup2` to `CHILD_BOOTSTRAP_DESCRIPTOR` (3) and `CHILD_CONTROL_DESCRIPTOR` (4) clobbers both ends; a failed `exec` then writes nowhere, the parent reads EOF and `spawn` returns `Ok`. Launch only fails later via the TLS deadline, so the no-silent-fail-open contract was broken.
- Fix: `SpawnReservation` (`crates/bitty-runtime/src/ai_publication_launch/unix.rs:79`) opens CLOEXEC placeholder pipes until a pair lands entirely above `HIGHEST_PLACEMENT_DESCRIPTOR` (=4, `unix.rs:67`). `pipe(2)` returns the two lowest free descriptors, so that terminating pair proves `0..=4` were occupied. The reservation is held across `Command::spawn` (`unix.rs:225`) and released by `after_spawn`/`close_child_ends` (`unix.rs:177`, `ai_publication_launch.rs:487`), `abort` (handles=None), and `Drop`.

### Security checks
- Range: placement targets 3/4 with a compile-time `bootstrap <= control` assertion (`unix.rs:70`); the reservation covers `0..=4`. fd 5 is documented as reserved for a later data channel and is not written today, so it needs no placeholder (see note).
- CLOEXEC: `pipe_with(CLOEXEC)` on Linux, `fcntl` on other Unix; a test asserts `O_CLOEXEC` and a `/proc/<pid>/fd` identity check proves no reservation inode crosses `exec`.
- No fd confusion: the reservation is never read/written and never moves existing fds; `place_child_descriptors` duplicates sources to >=10 before `dup2`, so a source cannot collide with a placement target.
- Failure cleanup: a partial reserve drops the `Vec` (closing all pipes) and returns typed `LaunchError::SpawnReservation` (`ai_publication_launch.rs:281`); `after_spawn`/`Drop` release the reservation; both are idempotent.
- Exec-error channel: the restored regression prints `spawn failed closed as required: No such file or directory (os error 2)` — the real `ENOENT`, not `EBADF`; a failed exec surfaces as `Err`.
- Deny path: the seam has no allow/deny branch; no behavior change beyond descriptor occupancy.

### Mutation proof
- Made `reserve()` return an empty `SpawnReservation` (exact pre-fix behavior): `nonexistent_executable_is_reported_when_placement_descriptors_are_free` fails with `spawn of a nonexistent executable reported success` (`tests.rs:496`) — fail-open reproduced.
- Restored: 21/21 `ai_publication_launch` tests pass.

### Gates
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- `cargo clippy -p bitty-runtime --features publication-control-test-support --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace --all-targets --locked`: exit 0.
- nextest feature suite: 21/21 passed.

### Residual risk (documented, non-blocking)
- A concurrent close of an already-occupied low descriptor between reservation and spawn reopens the window; the module documents the single-threaded launch-setup assumption. Acceptable while the seam is feature-gated and unwired; revisit when ai_helper wiring introduces concurrency.

### Non-blocking notes
- `HIGHEST_PLACEMENT_DESCRIPTOR` derives only from `CHILD_CONTROL_DESCRIPTOR` (`unix.rs:67`); when the fd-5 data-channel placement lands it must be raised (or derived from the highest placed descriptor).
- The guard test asserts `Err` but not the errno; asserting `raw_os_error() == ENOENT` would pin the exec-error contract further.

Root cause confirmed live: PTY forwarder wakes once on EOF, but Linux closes tty fds (exit_files) before the child is reapable (exit_notify); immediate waitpid misses 206/300. Fix: Arc<AtomicBool> reader EOF latch per session plus TerminalApp bounded post-EOF reap wake (10ms to 500ms), no blocking wait. Production residuals still present:

1. Spawn-thread late-child race: spawn_helper_bounded uses an unbounded mpsc::channel. If recv_timeout expires after the spawn thread already sent Ok(child) but before rx is dropped, the Child is dropped from the channel without kill/wait; one such child per stall can be leaked/zombified across repeated stalls. The claim "a child that arrives after the supervisor gave up is killed and reaped" holds only when send fails. Use sync_channel(0), or an accepted flag/deadline check, and contain the child in the thread.
2. Windows generation ordering is not safe: try_lock_slot is a no-op on non-Unix. A stale helper can read the sequence, be preempted, and rename its temp after a newer helper publishes, overwriting newer evidence. The acceptance "an older late helper cannot replace newer evidence" is not met on Windows. Implement a portable lock (for example an atomic create_new lock file with bounded retry, or LockFileEx) or obtain an explicit Windows exception.
3. EvidenceFailed loses the stderr report: HelperDelivery::deliver returns EvidenceFailed before spawning when next_attempt fails (state directory unusable or lock busy). persist_ledger then usually fails for the same reason, so the actual stall report is never written to stderr, unlike the previous helper behavior. Fall back to a no-slot stderr-only helper and record both outcomes.
4. try_wait error path: supervise_helper sets HelperFailed on try_wait Err and drops a possibly-live Child without kill/track; track_abandoned drops children beyond MAX_ABANDONED_CHILDREN, so unreaped zombies can exceed the cap across repeated stalls. Always kill/track or reap.
5. late_helper_after_timeout_cannot_replace_newer_evidence does not exercise its claim: the suspended shell is SIGKILLed at the 100 ms deadline, so its "sleep 1; mv" never runs; the test only proves supervisor temp removal. Generation ordering is covered by stale_generation_cannot_replace_newer_evidence and helper_rejects_a_stale_generation, but the PR-body claim is overstated.
6. The in-band delivery summary is appended after up to 64 thread rows and can be truncated by the 8 KiB cap; place it before the thread table or reserve space for it.
7. finish_stdin's retained-writer policy needs the test/design reconciled (see the CI failure): assert bounded (<=1) rather than zero and account for HelperFailed/skipped writers, or kill the helper process group so descendants cannot hold the pipe.

Remaining blocker (Windows ordering):

- PortableGate stale reclaim is not linearizable. try_acquire (crates/bitty-terminal/src/stall_watchdog.rs:1641-1660) checks expired() then remove_file() then create(). With a stale gate, waiters A and B can both see expired; B removes the old gate and creates its own; A then removes B's fresh gate and creates its own; both return Ok(true), so next_attempt and commit can run concurrently. release (:1693-1695) unconditionally removes the path, not just the caller's own gate, so a displaced/stale holder can delete a newer holder's gate. This is the dead-holder reclaim path, not only the documented "live holder stalled for seconds" exception. With two generations in flight, an older late helper can pass the generation check before a newer allocation/publish and then rename after it, overwriting newer evidence; the lease's 5 s window does not make the steal atomic. portable_gate_reclaims_only_an_expired_lease (:2916) is single-threaded and does not exercise concurrent reclaim/release. Fix: single-winner atomic steal (for example rename the stale gate to a unique quarantine path, so only one rename succeeds, then create) plus an owner token checked by release, or an OS lock; add a concurrent reclaim/release test. The PR residual documents live-holder displacement but not this concurrent dead-holder race.
- Minor test fragility: repeated_stalls snapshots pinned_before (around :3664) before supervise_helper; reap_finished can join a writer that finishes in that window, then a new writer is spawned while the test expects the pinned branch. 3/3 local and the prior CI full suites passed, but the assertion should use the actual spawn/skip result from start_stdin_writer instead of an external snapshot.

Re-review of Core PR #2567 head 3db89650 (merge of a63983a2 with main 2b894338; prior head 7eff34c7). Verdict: NEEDS-FIX.

1. Stale steal single-winner: verified. PortableGate now carries a unique owner token; RecoveryClaim (.recover) serializes reclaimers; the stale gate is moved with an atomic quarantine rename; the moved token is compared before publication. concurrent_stale_reclaim_has_one_winner is a real 6-thread/barrier test, passed 20/20 local runs, and checks exactly one winner, that losers and the displaced seed cannot delete the winner, and no .stale. leftovers. portable_gate_release_is_ownership_checked verifies token-checked release. This closes the previous check-remove-create race and unconditional release for the normal path.

2. NOT fully fixed: a displaced holder can still publish after a newer generation. In StateSlot::commit the ownership check is at line 1440, before read_attempt/stage; stage is line 1452 and publish is line 1453 with no second verify. StateSlot::publish (1320-1324) calls prepare, which only checks that the gate path is a regular owned file, not its token. A holder that passes verify, then stalls in stage/fsync past PORTABLE_GATE_STALE (5 s), can be displaced by a newer helper; when it resumes, its publish renames the old temp over the newer evidence. The supervisor's 250 ms kill does not help if the helper is in uninterruptible I/O (the documented best-effort case). The added test displaced_stale_holder_cannot_publish_after_newer_evidence (3322-3379) does not exercise this: it acquires and reclaims a gate, then calls slot.commit with a NEW PortalGate while new_gate is held; the old_gate is never used to stage/publish, and the test would still pass if lock.verify were removed. The Windows branch (3350-3356) only asserts that a new commit cannot acquire a fresh gate. Fix: add lock.verify() immediately before self.publish (or pass the SlotLock into publish and check its token), and add a probe that acquires the old SlotLock/gate, ages/reclaims it, stages the stale bytes, then publishes and asserts the newer slot survives. This is the remaining blocker.

3. Concurrent reclaim/release test is real: multiple threads (6 racers + seed), barrier-synchronized, with release of losers and seed; it targets the old multiple-winner check-remove-create behavior. 20/20 local repeats passed.

4. repeated_stalls_keep_helper_resources_bounded now uses the actual start_stdin_writer decision via runtime.writers/writers_skipped (2252, 2593) rather than an external pinned_before snapshot; it asserts exactly one spawn-or-skip per delivery, accepts TimedOut|HelperFailed, and checks the bounds. It passed 3/3 exact local runs plus the 48-test suite.

5. Merge conflict resolution is correct: crates/bitty-terminal/Cargo.toml has the nix feature union fs, poll, process, signal, term, user; CHANGELOG keeps the main Added entries and the #2560 Fixed entry; no conflict markers; stall_watchdog.rs is byte-identical to PR head a63983a2 (git diff --quiet), and the helper test/soak script are intact. Windows CI repair on c68f2f65 (PR #2567, not merged), monitor_soak_with_broken_stderr_keeps_phase_and_thread_evidence.
Root cause: test snapshot race, not a production ordering bug. write_report_to commits the state slot (StateSlot::commit -> stage/sync/rename) before it attempts stderr; the real helper uses the same function. The soak test asserted saw_state immediately after its poll observed the renamed slot, so on Windows the monitor thread could be between the rename and the stderr write when the assertion ran. Linux/macOS scheduling hid it.
Fix: BrokenStderr now records whether the slot existed at the first stderr write of the first delivery (first_write_seen / first_write_saw_state), and the test waits (bounded 5 s) for that write before asserting. This observes the real contract without sampling a snapshot; the per-write and post-shutdown checks remain.
Sensitivity: temporarily inverting write_report_to to stderr-first made the test fail at the new "evidence must be on disk before the first failing stderr write" assertion; restoring the order passes. No production change was needed.
